summary: The article examines how the rapid growth of mobile payments is increasing cyber risk for banks and financial institutions. It outlines challenges such as diverse payment systems (NFC, QR codes, peer-to-peer apps) and attack types like phishing and man-in-the-middle schemes. It then recommends strategies including strong authentication, regular patching, end-to-end encryption, real-time monitoring, customer education and industry information sharing.
one_line: Mobile payment growth raises financial cyber risk, and experts recommend authentication, patching, encryption, monitoring, customer education and collaboration as defenses.
key_facts: A Global Financial Security Board report published October 1, 2023 said mobile payment transactions grew 40% from the previous year.
Alice Chen, a cybersecurity analyst at the CyberFinance Institute, warned that "the intersection of finance and technology is fertile ground for cybercriminals."

Paul Harrison, head of Security at Unified Bank, said at a cybersecurity summit on November 16, 2023 that mobile payments are "dramatically altering the cybersecurity paradigm for financial institutions."
Mobile payment systems include contactless Near Field Communication (NFC) technologies, Quick Response (QR) codes, and peer-to-peer payment apps, each creating different vulnerabilities.
Mobile devices are personal and multifunctional, making them prone to attacks ranging from phishing to man-in-the-middle schemes.
Biometrics such as fingerprint and facial recognition, plus two-factor (2FA) and multi-factor authentication (MFA), are cited as key defenses for mobile payment apps.
Rebecca Silva of Digital Trust said "static passwords are no longer enough."
On September 30, 2023, MonetizeMe experienced a minor breach that was contained quickly thanks to its diligent update protocol.
Cindy Lau, MonetizeMe's Chief Technology Officer, said regular updates can be the difference between an averted threat and a full-blown data breach.
End-to-end encryption keeps payment data unreadable to anyone outside the transaction from initiation to processing.
On December 5, 2023, an anomaly detected by TrustFinance's monitoring system halted what could have been a massive data breach.
John Kramer, a cybersecurity consultant, argued that educating the public on secure mobile payment practices is crucial, since users may be the biggest vulnerability.
The article recommends partnerships between banks, payment service providers and cybersecurity firms to share threat information.
